name: metamodel.get
title: Show metamodel
summary: The effective metamodel: types with inherited properties and statuses, properties with whether they count to the version, relation kinds, statuses, meanings, the files read.

types.title: Types
types.description: The types with inheritance resolved (SR-012), in metamodel order; `statuses` are the statuses each type offers (ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#306).

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: The property definitions as written, except that each carries `content`, false when not written: whether a change of its value gives a new version and makes evidence and relations outdated (D-057, #624).

meanings.title: Meanings
meanings.description: Every built-in meaning of metamodel.schema.json (`meaning` of types, properties and relation kinds) -> the keys whose own definition declares it, in metamodel order; empty if unassigned (SR-013 AK3). In a valid metamodel a type or property meaning has at most one key, a relation meaning any number. Types that inherit a meaning, or repeat the one they inherit, are not listed; `types` shows their effective `meaning`.

relationKinds.title: Relation kinds by type

targetTypes.title: Target types
targetTypes.description: Every type of the metamodel a target may have, subtypes included, in metamodel order.

relationKinds.description: For each type of `types`, by its key: the relation kinds an element of that type may get, in metamodel order, each with the types its target may have, by the rule of relation.options, so an element of the type gets the same kinds there (SR-067). A new element has no reference to ask relation.options with.

files.title: Metamodel files
files.description: The metamodel files that were read, in the order they were merged, faulty ones included: the repository of the metamodel and the path relative to it (#625). Empty when the folder is missing or has no metamodel files.

uses.title: Uses

types.title: Types
types.description: Each type of `types`, in metamodel order, with the number of elements of the type.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Each property of `properties`, in metamodel order, with the number of elements of any type, also of a type the metamodel does not have, whose file holds its key, also with an empty value (SR-236 AK8): the use that locks a change of its value kind or several values.

count.title: Elements
count.description: Elements whose file holds the key of the property.

values.title: Fixed values
values.description: Each fixed value of each property with choices, in metamodel order, with the number of elements of any type whose value of the property is the choice or holds it (SR-236 AK7).

count.title: Elements
count.description: Elements whose value of the property is the choice or holds it.

relations.title: Relation kinds
relations.description: Each relation kind of `relations`, in metamodel order, with the number of elements whose file holds its key: a relation of the kind or an empty list.

count.title: Elements
count.description: Elements whose file holds the key of the relation kind.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: Each status of `statuses`, in metamodel order, with the number of elements of any type, also of a type the metamodel does not have, with that status (SR-236 AK8).

uses.description: The uses of each definition by the elements of the workspace, in any status (SR-236 AK7, AK8), counted over the element files on this machine that can be read; every definition is listed, 0 when unused. Each number is a number of elements: `element.list` with `selection.output` naming the number's field and entry gives the elements it counts (SR-224 AK4). A property and a status count on elements of any type (SR-236 AK8), so a definition that stays after its last type lost it shows the number of elements that keep it (SR-240 AK3, SR-238 AK5). A removal or a change that only works without use is refused while its use is above 0, while a repository of the workspace is not on this machine, and while an element file cannot be read (SR-236 AK7). Removing a property or a status from a type counts only the elements of the types that lose it (the type and the types that extend it), so it can succeed while the count shown here is above 0.
